findings.evidence: Lines 349, 358, 367 each name `lMuNuVA` as a rewrite/simp target; `grep -n 'lMuNuVA_def' EpsilonEridani/` returns nothing. The `:= (rfl)` idiom is already used for `bilinMap_apply` (Alternating/BilinMap.lean:54).
findings.fix: Add `lemma lMuNuVA_def (g) (ε) (K) (cV cA) : lMuNuVA g ε K cV cA = (cV ^ 2 + cA ^ 2) • lMuNu g K + (2 * cV * cA) • lMuNuOdd ε K := (rfl)` and rewrite with it in those three proofs instead of unfolding `lMuNuVA`.
findings.issue: `lMuNuVA` has only the pointwise `lMuNuVA_apply`; there is no form-level `lMuNuVA_def`. Consequently `lMuNuVA_flip` (line 349), `inv_two_smul_lMuNuVA_add_flip` (line 358) and `inv_two_smul_lMuNuVA_sub_flip` (line 367) all reach for the body (`simp only [lMuNuVA]` / `rw [..., lMuNuVA]`), and any consumer doing `Bilin`-level algebra must do the same — which only works because the file sits under `@[expose] public section` (line 79).

findings.evidence: BilinMap.lean:57 `@[simp] theorem bilinMap_apply_self`, versus lines 69 and 74 with no attribute; the downstream specializations `lMuNuOdd_apply_k_left_eq_zero` etc. are all `@[simp]` (Tensors/Basic.lean:277,282,287,292).
findings.fix: Tag both with `@[simp]`. Their LHSs `f.bilinMap m (m i) w` / `f.bilinMap m v (m i)` are ordinary first-order patterns; they cannot loop, and they do not fire on the `lMuNuOdd` instantiation (where the argument is `K.k`, not `![K.k, K.kPrime] 0`), so the specialized simp lemmas at Tensors/Basic.lean:277-294 stay in normal form.
findings.issue: `bilinMap_apply_left_eq_zero` (line 69) and `bilinMap_apply_right_eq_zero` (line 74) are the characteristic vanishing lemmas of `bilinMap` but carry no `@[simp]`, while the third vanishing lemma `bilinMap_apply_self` (line 57) does. A user of the general API gets `simp` closing `f.bilinMap m v v = 0` but stuck on `f.bilinMap m (m i) w = 0`.

summary: Surface is minimal with no compatibility artifacts and no hidden general infrastructure, but `lMuNuVA` has no unapplied `*_def` lemma — three proofs in the file unfold the definition instead — and the two general vanishing lemmas of `AlternatingMap.bilinMap` lack `@[simp]` while their sibling `bilinMap_apply_self` carries it.
